sections.title: Expressing Futile Attempts with hiába
sections.content: *Hiába* ('in vain, no matter how much') is new here: it says that an effort did not bring the result you wanted, and the main clause then says what stayed the same: *Hiába érveltek órákon át, a bizottság nem változtatta meg a határozatot.* It needs an effort or an action: *hiába* does not fit a plain fact such as the weather.

items.spanish: Hiába érveltek órákon át, a bizottság nem változtatta meg a határozatot.
items.english: No matter how much they argued for hours, the committee did not change the resolution.

items.spanish: Hiába érveltek a képviselők, a javaslatot nem fogadták el.
items.english: No matter how much the representatives argued, the proposal was not adopted.
